codeReview.summary: The implementation is scoped correctly: it adds `"chicken"` to the renumbering allowlist, commits chicken heavy/lambda germline tables plus a new lambda Stockholm/HMM asset, and adds focused species-contract coverage around heavy-chain renumbering and germline assignment. I found no high-confidence blocking defect in the product code, but the new tests are weaker than the H/L support contract they are meant to prove.

issues.description: `test_chicken_hmms_load_successfully()` only checks that at least one loaded HMM name contains `"chicken"`. The feature claims chicken H/L support and commits `chicken_L.hmm`/`chicken_L.sto`, but no assertion proves that both `chicken_H` and `chicken_L` load, and no chicken lambda sequence is exercised, so a broken lambda path could still slip through.

`test_chicken_vh_produces_numbered_result()` uses `result.shape[1] > 5` as a proxy for successful Kabat numbering. VAL-EXP-005 calls for valid numbered output, and that shape check can pass from metadata columns alone without proving any numbered residue positions were populated.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared mission state says where chicken germline FASTA inputs live, but it does not document how to derive the 128-character `all_germlines` amino-acid entries from IMGT gapped nucleotide FASTA or what filtering rules are acceptable for pseudogenes/fragments. This worker spent a large portion of the transcript reverse-engineering dot/codon handling, left/right padding, and filtering heuristics.

summary: Pass. The feature successfully wires chicken into the renumbering allowlist and adds heavy/lambda germline assets, with only non-blocking gaps in the strength of the new contract tests (especially around lambda-chain proof and numbered-position assertions).
